Class ProductServer.ClientHandler

java.lang.Object
com.robuschi.ProductServer.ClientHandler
All Implemented Interfaces:
Runnable
Enclosing class:
ProductServer
private class ProductServer.ClientHandler extends Object implements Runnable

The ClientHandler class handles individual client connections in a separate thread.

Manages the socket connection for every user, the input and output streams, their authentication status and their username.

All the messages that have to be sent to the clients are managed using this class.

Author:
Mattia Robuschi Caprara

    • handleMessage

      private void handleMessage(Protocol.Message message) throws IOException

      Handles all the messages that receives from the login form and the user client.

      • If the received message has type AUTH_REQUEST the handleAuthentication() is called
      • If the received message has type GET_PRODUCTS the handleGetProducts() is called
      • If the received message has type PURCHASE_PRODUCT the handlePurchase() is called
      • If the received message has type RETURN_PRODUCT the handleReturn() is called
      • If the received message has type ADD_NEW_PRODUCT the handleAddProduct() is called
      • If the received message has type USER_LOGOUT the handleUserLogout() is called
      • If the received message has type CLOSE the handleClose() is called
      Parameters:
      message - based on this parameters it uses a switch-case to determinate which method has to use based on the request
      Throws:
      IOException - based on the exceptions that the methods used inside this method throws in return
      See Also:
      • Protocol.MessageType

    • handleAuthentication

      private void handleAuthentication(Protocol.Message message) throws IOException

      This method is called when the client makes an authentication attempt.

      After pressing on the login button in the dedicated form, it sends this message, and if the authentication is successful the user can access the main page of the client.

      If the credentials used by the user are incorrect it sends a message to the clients which states that the authentication attempt failed.

      It sends out a message of type AUTH_SUCCESS to the client if the authentication is successful, otherwise it sends out a message of type AUTH_FAILED.

      Parameters:
      message - contains the type and payload which in this case is the couple username and password
      Throws:
      IOException - +

    • handleGetProducts

      private void handleGetProducts() throws IOException

      This method is called when the product list of the client needs to be updated.

      Usually called when we want to broadcast the changes in the list.

      It sends out a message of type PRODUCT_LIST to the client stating that it has to update its local list.

      Throws:
      IOException

    • handlePurchase

      private void handlePurchase(Protocol.Message message) throws IOException

      This method is called when a user tries to buy a product.

      Using the synchronized products list, it removes the product from the general product list and sends out a message to the client with the product as the payload so that the client can add it to its personal product list.

      If the general product list is not updated in the client and the user tries to buy a product that is not in the list anymore, this method sends out a message of type ERROR telling that the product is not available anymore.

      If the removal is successful it launches the broadcastProductList() method so that every client can update their server's product list.

      It sends out a message of type PRODUCT_PURCHASED to the client indicating that it can update its product list with the product that has bought.

      Parameters:
      message - contains the message type and the payload, which in this case is the product that the user wants to buy
      Throws:
      IOException

    • handleReturn

      private void handleReturn(Protocol.Message message) throws IOException

      This method is called when a user tries to return a product.

      It gets the product that the user wants to return from the message payload and adds it back to the server product list.

      It then launches the broadcastProductList() method so that every client can update their server's product list.

      It sends out a message of type RETURN_ACCEPTED to the client stating that return process was successful and the client product list can be updated.

      Parameters:
      message - contains the message type and the payload, which in this case is the product that the user wants to return
      Throws:
      IOException

    • handleAddProduct

      private void handleAddProduct(Protocol.Message message) throws IOException

      This method is called when the user wants to add a product to the server's product list.

      It gets the product (ID, Name, Price) from the message payload, then it adds it to the server's product list.

      It then launches the broadcastProductList() method so that every client can update their server's product list.

      Parameters:
      message - contains the message type and the payload, which in this case is the product that the user wants to add to the product list
      Throws:
      IOException
